name: ACS712ELCTR-05B-T
title: Hall-effect linear current sensor, ±5 A to ±30 A, 2.4 kVRMS isolated, SOIC-8
summary: A current sensor in an SOIC-8: the measured current flows through a 1.2 mΩ copper path on pins 1-4, and a Hall circuit on the die beside it turns the field into a voltage on pin 7. Pins 1-4 are insulated from the signal pins 5-8 to 2.4 kVRMS. It runs from a single 5 V supply; the output sits at VCC/2 with no current and is ratiometric to VCC. Three ranges are offered: ±5 A at 185 mV/A, ±20 A at 100 mV/A and ±30 A at 66 mV/A. A capacitor on FILTER sets the bandwidth, up to 80 kHz.
key_figures: 4.5 V to 5.5 V; 10 mA typ, 13 mA max
2400 VRMS for 60 s; 420 VPK / 297 VRMS working, basic

notes: Other packing is available from Allegro on request.
-S: lead-free build, with solder bumps based on tin-silver.
-T: build with lead-based solder bumps; RoHS compliant through the Annex III and IV exemptions of Directive 2011/65/EU (7(a), 15, 15(a), as they apply). -T and -S parts perform the same.
The suffix of each part number gives its range: x05B covers ±5 A, x20A ±20 A, x30A ±30 A.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The sensed current runs through pins 1-2 and out of pins 3-4; the signal side runs from +5 V. VIOUT sits at half the supply with no current and moves up or down in proportion to current in either direction, AC or DC. CBYP decouples VCC. CF on FILTER sets the bandwidth and so the noise; its value suits the application.

circuits.title: Peak detecting circuit
circuits.description: The sensor output passes through RF (10 kΩ) and COUT (0.1 µF), so only the AC part reaches VOUT, which R1 (1 MΩ) holds at ground on average. An LT1178 amplifier with D1 in its output and R3/R2 feedback (330 kΩ over 33 kΩ, a gain of 11) charges C1 to the peak of the swing; R4 (10 kΩ) carries that peak onto C2 at VPEAK. A 2N7002 across C2, driven at VRESET, empties it to restart the measurement. CF is 1 nF.

circuits.title: Output amplified to 610 mV/A
circuits.description: An LM321 amplifier, biased at mid-supply by R1 and R2 (100 kΩ each) on its non-inverting input, takes the sensor output through RF (1 kΩ) into its inverting input, with R3 (3.3 kΩ) and C1 (1000 pF) in parallel from output back to that input. The gain of 3.3 raises the sensitivity to 610 mV/A, a figure measured with an ACS712ELC-05A; C1 rolls off the top end. CF is 0.01 µF.
notes: LM321 pins: 1 IN+, 2 V-, 3 IN-, 4 OUT, 5 V+.

circuits.title: Rectified output for an A-to-D converter
circuits.description: RF (2 kΩ) and R1 (10 kΩ) divide the sensor output down for a 3.3 V converter; D1 (1N4448W) rectifies the divided signal, and C1 at the converter input filters it. It takes the place of a current transformer. C1 is chosen for the converter's load and the smoothing wanted; R1 is left off when the whole output range is to be kept. CF is 1 nF.

circuits.title: 10 A overcurrent fault latch
circuits.description: An LMV7235 comparator watches the sensor output on its inverting input against a threshold from R1 (33 kΩ) and R2 (100 kΩ) on its non-inverting input; RPU (100 kΩ) pulls its open-drain output up to 5 V. When the output passes the threshold the comparator pulls Fault low, and D1 (1N914) drags the threshold node low with it, so the fault stays latched until the 5 V supply is removed. CF is 1 nF.
notes: LMV7235 pins: 1 OUT, 2 V-, 3 IN+, 4 IN-, 5 V+.

operation.text: Current in the copper path close to the die surface makes a magnetic field, and a low-offset, chopper-stabilized BiCMOS Hall circuit turns it into a proportional voltage. Having the field source so close to the Hall element is what gives the accuracy. Each part is programmed for accuracy after packaging, and every part is calibrated at the factory before shipping.
Current flowing from pins 1 and 2 to pins 3 and 4 drives the output above VIOUT(Q); current the other way drives it below. AC and DC currents are both measured.

The path is 1.2 mΩ typical, so it dissipates little. Its copper is thick enough to survive five times the rated current. Its terminals are electrically insulated from pins 5 to 8, so the sensor gives isolation without an optocoupler.
Both the zero-current output (nominally VCC/2) and the sensitivity scale with VCC. The two ratiometric-change equations measure how closely they follow it.

Output change for a 1 A change in primary current: the magnetic coupling (G/A) times the gain of the linear amplifier (mV/G). The gain is set at the factory for the full-scale current of each version.
Amplifier gain times the Hall noise floor of about 1 G, which comes from thermal and shot noise in the Hall element.
How far the output departs from proportional over the full-scale range. Saturation of the flux concentrator near full-scale current is a cause.

VIOUT(Q) is the output at zero primary current, nominally VCC/2; it varies with the resolution of the quiescent trim and with thermal drift. The electrical offset VOE is the part of the departure from VCC/2 that has a non-magnetic cause.

ETOT is the largest departure of the output from its ideal value. Accuracy is considered at four points: zero current at 25 °C, zero current over temperature, full-scale current at 25 °C, and full-scale current over temperature.
tPO is counted from when the supply passes VCC(min) to when the output, with a field applied, settles to within ±10 % of its final value. It grows with the FILTER capacitor.
tr runs from 10 % to 90 % of full-scale output after a current step. Eddy currents in the conductive ground plane of the IC slow both tr and the response time.

The Hall signal is modulated so that the DC offset of the element and its amplifier lands at a different frequency from the field signal; after demodulation a low-pass filter removes the offset. A sample-and-hold, clock logic and a regulator support it. The output therefore drifts very little with temperature and package stress and recovers well after temperature cycling.

An RC low-pass on the output of a sensor improves resolution, but its series resistor forms a divider with the load resistance and attenuates even DC, by an amount that changes with temperature as the two resistances drift apart. Inside the ACS712 the 1.7 kΩ filter resistor comes before a buffer amplifier, and the FILTER pin brings out the node between them, so a capacitor CF from FILTER to ground filters the signal without that attenuation.
VIOUT drives at most 10 nF and no less than 4.7 kΩ to GND.

The leadframe is plated in 100 % matte tin for lead-free board assembly. Inside, the -T parts use high-temperature lead-based flip-chip solder bumps under a RoHS exemption; the -S parts use tin-silver bumps.

Named uses: motor control, sensing and managing loads, switch-mode supplies, and protecting against overcurrent faults, in industrial, commercial and communications equipment. Not intended for automotive use.
TÜV America certificate numbers U8V 15 05 54214 038 and CB 13 06 54214 026.
The reference land pattern follows IPC7351 SOIC127P600X175-8M, with every pad at least 0.20 mm from its neighbours; it is adjusted to suit the assembly process and board tolerances.

Top face, three lines: the part number (8 characters), temperature, package and current (8 characters), and the first 5 characters of the assembly lot number; pin 1 is marked by a dot. The underside carries the country of origin and lot number.
